title: Staged Safe-Apply: Predictive divergence detection and economic fallback playbook
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Implement an automated, staged safe-apply system that performs predictive dry-runs, detects configuration-induced divergence (performance/cost/regression), and executes economically-aware fallback policies. The feature must support shadow applies, staged checkpoints, and a fast automated rollback when predefined safety signals are triggered. This ticket covers design, implementation hooks in the config-applier service, operator controls in the Console, and observability/telemetry required for safe automation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A safe-apply flow exists which can run a non-impacting dry-run that simulates new config against a replay of recent requests. 2) A divergence detector computes an economic impact score (0-100) and flags changes > 35 as candidate rollbacks. 3) Automated rollback triggers if any of: cost-per-token delta > +12%, P99 latency delta > +30ms, 5xx rate delta > +0.4%, or KV-cache hit-rate drop > 15% sustained over 5 minutes. 4) Console shows staged progress (0%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with per-stage telemetry and explicit approval or auto-rollback outcome. 5) System records a signed state checkpoint before apply and can replay to restore exact runtime state in <= 90s for Dedicated pools. 6) End-to-end tests and a synthetic workload validated on staging with documented PR and runbook.
design_notes: Overview: Add a 'staged-safe-apply' mode to the config-applier. Steps: 1) Preflight: run a dry-run that replays a sliding window (last 15m) of real requests into a sandbox of the target model and hardware profile; collect metrics (tokens, latency, errors, kv-cache stats). 2) Scoring: compute an economic impact score combining estimated token cost delta, avg latency delta weighted by request importance, and cache-hit delta. 3) Shadow Apply: for the first stage, route 0% traffic but create runtime artifacts (weights, quantized kernels, batch configs) and measure synthetic hits. 4) Staged Traffic Ramp: increment stage percentages with canary windows and continuous divergence monitoring. 5) Reconciliation: maintain a checkpointed state blob (versioned config + KV-prefix snapshots) that can be applied atomically to revert to pre-change state. Implementation details: use existing prefix-caching exporter, extend the telemetry schema to include 'apply_id', instrument kernel selection metrics, and add RPC hooks to runtime to quiesce and snapshot active KV caches. Cost-model: integrate with Optimize service to estimate cost-per-token for both baseline and candidate config. Avoid blocking tenant traffic; all reversible ops must be idempotent. Security: apply audit log entries for every stage.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): dry-run and replay harness — 1 week. Phase 1 (internal canary): 10% internal apps for 48h, manual approval required to proceed. Phase 2 (low-risk customers): 25% for 24h with auto-rollback enabled. Phase 3 (general availability): full rollout with auto-rollback and 2-minute operator alerting window. Operators may opt-in to manual gates per release. Monitor dashboards: cost-impact, latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, kv-cache hit/miss trends. Ship as runtime-1.20 behind Console feature flag.
telemetry: Emit metrics with labels {apply_id, stage, model_version, pool_id}: cost_estimate_delta (ratio), cost_impact_score (0-100), p50/p95/p99_latency_delta_ms, error_rate_delta_pct, kv_cache_hit_rate_delta_pct, synthetic_request_success. Traces: attach a sampled trace for canonical replay requests with tag apply_id. Logs: structured audit entries for each staged mutation with before/after config diff and checkpoint_id. Alerts: fire on thresholds and create a PagerDuty alert with runbook link.
